text: Thin-film lithium niobate (LNOI) modulators outperform silicon plasma-dispersion modulators for high-speed data encoding mainly because the Pockels effect is:
choices: A pure, linear refractive-index change that is low-loss and essentially chirp-free (alpha_H ~ 0)
A carrier-based effect that adds optical loss and chirp, just like silicon
explanation: The Pockels effect changes index linearly with applied field without injecting or depleting carriers, so it adds essentially no loss or chirp and supports >100 GHz bandwidth. Adding loss and chirp describes silicon's plasma dispersion (the opposite); LNOI is not bandwidth-limited to 1 GHz and does not rely on thermal tuning for modulation.
